summary.text: Tom Cotton is the Republican nominee and incumbent U.S. Senator from Arkansas, seeking a third term. A Harvard-educated lawyer and Army infantry officer who served in Iraq and Afghanistan, he worked as a management consultant, served one term in the U.S. House, and has been in the Senate since 2015, where he chairs the Select Committee on Intelligence and the Senate Republican Conference.

paragraphs.text: Born in Dardanelle, Arkansas, in 1977. According to his official Senate biography, he grew up on his family's cattle farm in Yell County and graduated from Dardanelle High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree in government from Harvard University in 1998 and a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 2002.
Worked as a law clerk for the U.S. Court of Appeals and in private law practice before leaving the law after the September 11 attacks to join the Army, according to his official biography.

Served nearly five years on active duty in the U.S. Army (2004-2009) as an infantry officer, including combat tours in Iraq with the 101st Airborne and in Afghanistan with a Provincial Reconstruction Team, and service with The Old Guard at Arlington National Cemetery. His decorations include the Bronze Star Medal, the Combat Infantryman Badge and the Ranger Tab.
Worked for McKinsey & Co. as a management consultant and, per Ballotpedia, also as a farmer, between leaving the Army and entering Congress.
Served one term in the U.S. House of Representatives for Arkansas's 4th District (2013-2015).
Was elected to the U.S. Senate in 2014, defeating incumbent Democrat Mark Pryor, and was re-elected in 2020 over Ricky Dale Harrington Jr.

In the Senate he serves on the Armed Services Committee, the Energy and Natural Resources Committee, and the Joint Economic Committee, and chairs the Select Committee on Intelligence. He is also Chairman of the Senate Republican Conference, the third-ranking position in Senate Republican leadership.
According to his official biography, he and his wife Anna have two sons, Gabriel and Daniel.
